title: Where Should a Stuck Agent Spend Its Next Tokens? Causal Attribution of Inference-Time Resources
abstract: arXiv:2610.28834v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Inference-time scaling is often treated as a token-budget problem, but a failed coding agent can seek qualitatively different resources: computation, information, or feedback. We introduce Banzhaf Resource Attribution (BRA), a controlled factorial framework that measures each resource's marginal contribution to repair and its interactions while holding the failed state and revision protocol fixed. We evaluate six models on 194 function-level failures from MBPP+ and HumanEval+ and 126 repository-level failures from SWE-bench Verified. Task-relevant specifications consistently improve repair, whereas public-test feedback provides small gains and retrieved code little to none. The value of additional computation declines with model capability, while information remains useful; resource channels largely exhibit diminishing returns, although complementary information can reinforce itself. translated_title: 陷入困境的智能体应该把接下来的令牌花在哪里？推理时资源的因果归因
translated_abstract: 推理时扩展通常被视为令牌预算问题，但一个失败的编码智能体可以寻求性质不同的资源：计算、信息或反馈。我们提出了班扎夫资源归因，这是一个受控的因子实验框架，在保持失败状态和修订协议固定的情况下，测量每种资源对修复的边际贡献及其交互作用。我们在MBPP+和HumanEval+的194个函数级失败以及SWE-bench Verified的126个仓库级失败上评估了六个模型。任务相关的规范始终能改善修复效果，而公开测试反馈仅带来小幅提升，检索到的代码几乎没有作用。额外计算的价值随模型能力的增强而下降，而信息仍然有用；资源通道大多表现出收益递减，尽管互补信息可以自我强化。然而，四个前沿模型中有三个选择了反馈……
tldr: 提出班扎夫资源归因框架，通过受控因子实验因果地量化计算、信息、反馈等推理时资源对修复失败编码任务的边际贡献，发现任务相关规范最有价值、额外计算的价值随模型能力递减，而多数前沿模型却错误地将预算分配给收益甚微的反馈资源。
en_tdlr: Introduces Banzhaf Resource Attribution (BRA), a controlled factorial framework that causally quantifies the marginal contribution of computation, information, and feedback resources for repairing failed coding agents, finding that task-relevant specifications are most valuable while frontier models misallocate their budgets toward low-yield feedback.
